Subject: Private offer questions — bucket increments & partner payout timing

Hi David,

Thanks for the draft private offer. A couple quick clarifying questions from procurement and our partner team before we loop legal:

1) Incremental buckets — the offer shows 4 usage buckets with % discounts that step at monthly thresholds (e.g., >50k token-hours). Do you support more granular increments during ramp (e.g., 10k, 20k) and can those be applied retroactively within a billing month or only prospectively?

2) Reseller timing — our reseller (CloudBroker) needs a clear payout cadence to align cashflow. Is Redwood able to commit to a 30-day payout from invoice date for pass-through commissions, or is the standard 60-day?

3) Evidence for channel margin — procurement asked for the expected reseller netback table you promised. Can you attach the breakdown?

If you can respond today, we can keep the legal window tight.

Appreciate it —
Aaron
Senior SRE, Fennel Technologies

Subject: Re: Private offer questions — bucket increments & partner payout timing

Aaron — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front then attaching the matrices you asked for.

- Incremental buckets: We can support finer-grained tiers (10k/20k) for the initial 3 months of the contract as a ramp guarantee. Those are applied prospectively for the remainder of the month, but we can offer a one-time retroactive true-up at month close if you hit the higher threshold within that billing period. The true-up would be limited to the month of occurrence (i.e., not a rolling retrospective).

- Reseller payout cadence: Standard is 60-day net for marketplace settlements, but for strategic partners / named reseller deals we can commit to 30-day pass-through with a short payment protection clause (if Redwood hasn't received marketplace funds within 45 days, we reserve a short reconciliation window). We documented the clause in the attached "Reseller_Payout_Schedule.pdf".

- Channel margin table: attached "PrivOffer_SKU_Matrix.xlsx" contains per-SKU list price, Redwood net (post-discount), and suggested reseller netback for three commission models (percentage, fixed per-node, hybrid).

Next steps I propose:
- Vanessa and I will sync with CloudBroker on expected invoice flows.
- If that aligns, we'll update the DocuSign and send an Addendum that includes the 10k ramp tiers and the 30-day reseller payout language for signature.

Attaching: PrivOffer_SKU_Matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
           Reseller_Payout_Schedule.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the table.

-David Kim
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

Hey Aaron — looping in Kimberly from Partner Ops to confirm operational implications. A few operational notes below: 

- Our marketplace export cadence (what we receive from AWS/GCP/Azure) is typically 30-45 days post month-end depending on the provider. That is why the default is 60-day net. If we sign the 30-day pass-through, CloudBroker must accept the reconciliation clause: Redwood will pay 30 days after we receive funds from the marketplace; if marketplace delays extend beyond 45 days, Redwood will notify and initiate a one-time 15-day provisional settlement with an offset reconciliation on next invoice.

- For bucket true-ups: Partner Ops will need the usage reporting (daily CSV or API) from your side to validate thresholds. Can CloudBroker confirm they can push daily usage exports into our partner pipeline endpoint? Maya — can you confirm?

- For bookkeeping: to avoid double-counting, we prefer pass-through commissions as a separate line item on the invoice and not embedded in the SKU list price. The spreadsheet included two views; Kimberly will advise which view we should lock.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Aaron / Maya — quick operational confirmation and proposed language for the addendum below.

1) Payout cadence — proposed clause: 
"Redwood agrees to remit reseller commissions to CloudBroker within 30 calendar days of Redwood's receipt of corresponding marketplace funds. If Redwood's receipt of funds from the marketplace is delayed beyond 45 days from the end of the applicable usage month, Redwood will notify CloudBroker and remit a provisional payment (not to exceed 80% of estimated commission) within 60 days; any shortfall will be reconciled on the following invoice."

2) Ramp tiers & true-up — proposed: 
"For the first three (3) months following effective date, Redwood will apply ramped bucket thresholds at 10k/20k/50k token-hours. If actual usage during a billing month reaches a higher tier, Redwood will perform a retroactive true-up limited to that billing month only, and apply the higher tier pricing for that month. No retroactive true-ups will be applied beyond the month of occurrence."

3) Evidence / reporting required: daily usage feed (CSV or API), monthly invoice export from marketplace, and reseller payout statement. CloudBroker must deliver daily usages to partner-ops@redwood.ai by 13:00 PT each day.

If these three items look good to Fennel + CloudBroker, I'll draft the addendum and Vanessa can pull legal in for a 24-hour review.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Partner Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
